subject: DPA: log TTL and backup purge coordination
messages:
From: Audrey Liang <audrey.liang@medtechinc.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medtechinc.com
Date: Wed, 30 Apr 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: log TTL and backup purge coordination

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward finalizing the DPA, a few outstanding items from our side that we need to resolve before legal can sign:

- Backup purge cadence: we need clarity on how quickly backups that contain customer data are purged after deletion requests (both for EU-region data and cross-border subprocessor flows).
- Log retention exceptions: for clinical investigation troubleshooting we occasionally need extended forensic logs beyond our standard 90-day window; can Redwood support a documented exception process and temporary holds?
- Subprocessor visibility: please provide a current list of subprocessors that will process MediTech data (and which ones have access to backups/archival stores).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can (a) offer a controlled, auditable exception path for log retention (including who approves it and how long), and (b) provide an updated subprocessor file and a proposed amendment to the DPA covering backup purge timelines and forensic retain windows?

If useful, we can hop on a 30-minute call — our legal / security folks are on standby but wanted to get something in writing first.

Best,
Audrey
Audrey Liang
Senior Privacy Counsel
MediTech Inc.

Attachment: (none in this message)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Audrey Liang <audrey.liang@medtechinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 May 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: log TTL and backup purge coordination

Hi Audrey —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up-front: yes, we can provide a subprocessor export and draft an amendment that explicitly documents backup purge cadence and an exception approval flow for extended log retention. A few clarifying points so we scope properly:

1) Desired forensic retention window: you mentioned "occasionally" — can you give an example duration you expect (e.g., 9 months, 18 months)? That will determine storage tiers and cost.
2) Approval authority: we typically require a joint written approval (customer security lead + Redwood security/product manager) and a scoped justification (case ID, timebox). We can make that a formal ticketable workflow.
3) Cross-border note: for EU data we have regionally isolated snapshots; any exception that requires cross-border movement will need an amended SCCs/DPA clause.

Next steps proposed from Redwood side:
- I'll loop in Karthik (security) to draft the technical impacts and an exception playbook.
- Marissa will export the current subprocessor list and indicate which subprocessors touch backups or snapshot archives.
- We will produce a DPA amendment outline (backup purge cadence + exception workflow) for your review.

Can you confirm a target retention window (in days) and whether MediTech prefers the exception to be: (A) per-incident temporary hold (time-limited), or (B) standing exception for a named retention class (longer-term but documented)?

Irene Choi
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

On May 1, 2025, at 10:12 AM, Audrey Liang <audrey.liang@medtechinc.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Irene. We typically ask for a standing exception to 450 days for clinical investigation logs, but prefer per-incident holds for other cases. Happy to clarify on a quick call.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Audrey Liang <audrey.liang@medtechinc.com>
Date: Thu, 1 May 2025 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: log TTL and backup purge coordination

Irene / Marissa / Audrey —

Thanks for flagging; technical notes and proposal below.

Technical constraints and options:
- Primary production logs (ingress/traces/kv-access) are in a hot OLAP store and default to 90 days. Extending to 450 days for a named customer is feasible but will move data into an indexed cold tier (S3 IA + archival hot index). Query latency for ad-hoc forensics will increase and we should document expected SLA (e.g., 24–72 hours to provide a full forensic bundle).
- Backups and snapshots: incremental snapshots are retained per-region for 30 days by default; full snapshot images are tombstoned and purged at 60 days. We can create a scoped exception to hold snapshot images for up to 18 months under a locked access policy (separate KMS key).
- Access & auditing: any exception will require (1) a documented justification and case id, (2) approval by Redwood Security lead and MediTech Security contact, and (3) an immutable audit trail (we use write-once metadata and attach the approval record to the snapshot object).

Impact matrix (high level): see attached.
Proposal (recommended):
1) Standing exception class "Clinical Investigation" — 450 day log retention (cold tier) + 12 month snapshot hold (locked key).
2) Per-incident temporary hold — up to 30 days additional retention on logs/snapshots with explicit closure criteria.
3) Operational SLA — Redwood to fulfill forensic export within 72 hours; if expedited (within 24 hours) we charge an expedited ops fee.

I'll attach the retention-impact matrix and a sample approval template. If MediTech is good with the standing exception for clinical investigations we can incorporate the language into the DPA amendment and list the technical constraints.

—Karthik

Attachment: log-retention-impact-matrix.pdf

From: Audrey Liang <audrey.liang@medtechinc.com>

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. MediTech is prepared to accept the proposed model: standing exception for "Clinical Investigation" (450 days logs, 12 months snapshots) and per-incident temporary holds otherwise.

I've attached the current subprocessor list (CSV) and a redline proposal for the DPA amendment. Please review and let us know if Redwood needs different drafting to capture the operational controls (KMS key segregation, approval flow, audit trail).

We'll also need an internal contact at Redwood who will approve any per-incident holds — can you confirm the title/role and an escalation path?

Audrey

Attachments: meditech_subproc_list.csv, dpa_amendment_draft.docx

3) Subprocessor mapping: Marissa to annotate the CSV with which subprocessors have backup/snapshot access, and mark any cross-border subprocessors — owner: Marissa Cole — deliverable by Mon 2025-05-05.

If that timeline works I'll move forward and share the draft.

Thanks again —
Irene Choi
